about: T-3710 (owner, 2026-11-20): the generated part of the Chicago 4D score, as ElevenLabs Music composition plans through fal (the owner picked ElevenLabs over MiniMax v2.5 and Stable Audio). The main theme is a FIXED recording the owner chose (THEME-FINAL-portage-main-title.mp3); the title, ident, stings and overtures are cut from or built around it, never regenerated. Themes and rules: the Chicago 4D Score doc (https://claude.ai/artifact/ACXQqZ3pvHqLpofx2ZuqUP). Nothing here is played by the app yet. Built by a script; re-run it rather than hand-editing.

cues.use: Theme suite; source for 1812 cues

positive_global_styles: year 1812 frontier fort on Lake Michigan
soft hand drum like a heartbeat

positive_local_styles: a solo Woodlands cedar flute, free and unhurried, an original melody that opens with the rising fifth D to A, dignified and still
soft strings and harp beneath the flute, a hand drum like a slow heartbeat
the flute alone again, a long final note

cues.use: Theme suite; the river and lake

positive_local_styles: a rolling six-eight ostinato in harp and low strings, like a river current
a warm clarinet and horn line over the current that hints at the Portage hook
the current widens into shimmering strings, the river meeting the lake

cues.use: Theme suite; Fort Dearborn

positive_global_styles: year 1812 frontier fort on Lake Michigan
soft hand drum like a heartbeat

positive_local_styles: a crisp fife and rope-tension snare play a dotted garrison duty call
horns and strings take the call up as a proud small march, about 112 beats per minute
the fife plays the call once more, softer, as at day's end

cues.use: Theme suite; loss and memory

positive_local_styles: a solo cello plays the Portage hook slowly in D minor, noble and sorrowful
full strings take it, grief without blame
a quiet French horn and an open fifth to end

cues.use: Theme suite; mysteries and ghosts

positive_local_styles: celesta and low clarinet, a curious motif that bends through a tritone before settling, pizzicato basses
muted strings creep, a little eerie, never horror
the motif once more, ending on an unresolved chord
